title: X9C-2R Candidate Count Reconciliation
discrepancy_summary: X9C-2 summary table listed 4+20+10+5=39 bucket items, but reported 31 total candidates. Reconciliation reveals overlap in file-level counting.
overlap_explanation: The 31 route FILES contain policy-related code in at least one method, but individual FILES appear in multiple buckets because: (a) Some files have BOTH canonical-safe GET methods AND legacy POST/PATCH methods (e.g., engagements/route.ts is both 'canonical safe GET' and 'legacy POST'), (b) Some files have service dependencies across multiple handlers, (c) Some files have governance logic mixed with other patterns. Therefore, bucket counts (20+10+5=35 + 4 canonical=39) exceed unique file count (31) due to files appearing in multiple buckets.

reconciled_unique_items.reason: GET handler is already canonical safe with policy fallback. POST handler uses legacy pattern (withAuth).
GET handler is already canonical safe. PATCH handler uses legacy pattern.
GET handler is already canonical safe, no mutation methods.

reconciled_bucket_counts.accounting: 4 canonical safe files + 17 pure-legacy files + 10 service-dependent files = 31 unique files. (The 3 files with both canonical GET and legacy POST/PATCH are counted in 'canonical safe' bucket but POST/PATCH methods are also in 'legacy mutation' bucket.)

explanation_for_mismatch: X9C-2 reported 31 'candidates_found' from grep results (files with policy usage). The summary correctly shows 31 total. However, the summary TABLE lists buckets that overlap: 4 files with canonical safe GET methods also have legacy POST/PATCH methods, so they appear in both 'canonical safe' and 'legacy mutation' buckets. When buckets are counted: 20 legacy mutation routes (includes POST/PATCH from the 4 canonical GET files PLUS 16-17 additional files), 10 service-dependent, 5 governance-complex, 4 canonical-only = 39 if counted with overlap, but actually 31 unique files because of file-level overlap. The discrepancy (39 vs 31) is due to counting FILES in multiple buckets.

impact_for_x9c3_planning.critical_finding: 3-4 files currently have BOTH canonical safe GET handlers AND legacy mutation methods that need X9C-3+4 refactoring. When these files are migrated to full canonical pattern in X9C-4, the GET methods are already clean (no migration risk).
impact_for_x9c3_planning.service_refactor_scope: At least 10 files have service-dependent policy logic that must be addressed in X9C-3. Additionally, the 3-4 hybrid files' mutation methods also have service dependencies.

next_step: Use reconciled understanding to plan X9C-3 service boundary work carefully. Files with both canonical GET and legacy mutation need special attention to avoid introducing breaking changes to already-safe GET methods.
